c4d55f3c90.q: What is the CPR approach for worn dentition cases and how does it differ from traditional cosmetic dentistry workflows?
c4d55f3c90.a: CPR stands for Concept, Prototype, and Restoration. The key difference is that Dr. Hartlieb performs the prototype phase using reversible bonding on unprepared or minimally prepared teeth before committing to irreversible preparations. This allows dentists to work out functional, aesthetic, and phonetic issues without drilling, and patients can test-drive the new smile for typically three months before final restoration. This contrasts with traditional workflows where dentists move directly from mockup to definitive restorations after tooth preparation.

f97c702bd8.q: Why are composite bonding provisionals superior to porcelain veneer temporaries for diagnosing grinding habits?
f97c702bd8.a: Porcelain veneer provisionals frequently come off during the trial phase, making it impossible to reliably assess functional guidance issues and grinding behavior. With composite bonding prototypes, patients live with the proper tooth form for an extended period, allowing the dentist to discover grinding or other destructive habits naturally. If a patient claims not to grind but then chips the composite bonding overnight, this reveals their actual bruxism habit before expensive porcelain restorations are placed and destroyed.

6856d3d95c.q: What percentage of Dr. Hartlieb's prototype bonding cases do not include nightguards, and what is his reasoning?
6856d3d95c.a: Dr. Hartlieb does not make nightguards for approximately 50% of his prototype bonding cases. His philosophy is that patients fall into two groups: those who love nightguards and those who hate them. He leaves the decision to patients based on their history and willingness to wear one. If a patient refuses a nightguard, he prefers to observe what failures occur without it, as airway-compromised patients often dislike nightguards because the thickness suffocates them.

95dba08ef5.q: What records and imaging does Dr. Hartlieb obtain at the beginning of a worn dentition treatment case?
95dba08ef5.a: Initial records include full series of photographs, intraoral scans (Trios), and a face bow for analog wax-ups. Dr. Hartlieb also takes a bite registration in centric relation or seated joint position. If joint issues are suspected, a CBCT of the joints is taken. If airway concerns exist, a CBCT is obtained to provide airway information. He performs his own analog wax-ups on an articulator to identify occlusal and anatomical challenges before entering the patient's mouth.

b1c9575992.q: What is the advantage of composite bonding repairability compared to porcelain restorations for active patients?
b1c9575992.a: Composite bonding can be easily repaired by roughening the surface, adding new bonding material, and restoring it seamlessly. In contrast, porcelain restorations like Emax cannot be reliably repaired when chipped or fractured under functional load—any bonded repair will not withstand heavy chewing forces. Dr. Hartlieb prefers composite because it allows him to teach patients that destructive habits will ruin their dentistry, and when failures occur in the prototype phase, they are easily corrected rather than requiring full replacement.
